name: Winnipeg / James Armstrong Richardson International Airport
before:
Canada's seventh busiest airport by passengers, in Winnipeg, and the primary airport for a very large area that reaches into north western Ontario and Nunavut. It also serves numerous small remote communities across northern Manitoba on scheduled flights.

One detail makes a real difference to itineraries. Winnipeg is one of only nine Canadian airports with United States border pre-clearance, so a client flying on to the States clears US immigration before boarding rather than on arrival.

Daily non-stop flights reach destinations across Canada and the United States, with seasonal services to Mexico and the Caribbean. It is a hub for Calm Air, Perimeter Airlines and the cargo carrier Cargojet, a focus city for WestJet and a base for Flair Airlines.

The terminal was designed by the Argentine architect Cesar Pelli with Stantec, drawing on Manitoba's prairie and sky.

The airport shares its 1,370 hectare site with Canadian Forces Base Winnipeg.
after:
Canada's seventh busiest airport by passengers, in Winnipeg. Calm Air and Perimeter Aviation fly from here to communities across northern Manitoba and into north western Ontario and Nunavut.

One detail makes a real difference to itineraries. Winnipeg has United States border preclearance, so a client flying on to the States clears US border checks before boarding rather than on arrival.

Non-stop flights reach destinations in Canada and the United States, with seasonal services to the Caribbean. WestJet and Flair Airlines are among the carriers flying from here.

The terminal was designed by the Argentine-born architect Cesar Pelli with Stantec, drawing on Manitoba's prairie.

claims.claim: Canada's seventh busiest airport by passengers
claims.inAfter: Canada's seventh busiest airport by passengers
claims.note: Statistics Canada's 2025 table, released 21 July 2026, ranks Winnipeg seventh among all airports with a published figure: Toronto Pearson 45,998,881, Vancouver 26,013,167, Montreal-Trudeau 21,531,258, Calgary 18,803,183, Edmonton 7,658,691, Ottawa 4,732,563, Winnipeg 4,274,502, then Halifax 4,020,914 and Kelowna 2,244,830. Toronto Billy Bishop is suppressed for 2024 and 2025; its last published year (2023) was 2,000,714, less than half Winnipeg's, so it cannot be above. The table view and the full 2025 download are both Statistics Canada's table 23-10-0253-01 (one organisation).

claims.claim: Calm Air and Perimeter Aviation fly from here to communities in northern Manitoba, north western Ontario and Nunavut
claims.inAfter: Calm Air and Perimeter Aviation fly from here to communities across northern Manitoba and into north western Ontario and Nunavut.
claims.note: Replaces 'the primary airport for a very large area that reaches into north western Ontario and Nunavut' and 'serves numerous small remote communities across northern Manitoba on scheduled flights', and names the two airlines the old text called hubs. Calm Air's September 2026 timetable has Winnipeg flights to Thompson, Churchill and Rankin Inlet, and its own history places Rankin Inlet in Nunavut and describes Northern Manitoba service. Perimeter's timetable (effective 1 March 2026) has Winnipeg to Sandy Lake and Pikangikum, which its destination list puts in Ontario; 'north western Ontario' is Wikipedia's name for the region those communities are in. Perimeter's own name is Perimeter Aviation (the old text said Perimeter Airlines).

Canadian routes in 2026 include Porter's new Hamilton flights and its Ottawa flights (Airways, 29 January 2026) and Calm Air's Nunavut flights.

claims.claim: primary airport for a very large area
claims.wasBefore: and the primary airport for a very large area that reaches into north western Ontario and Nunavut
claims.why: 'Primary airport for a very large area' is Wikipedia's characterisation alone; the operator's site (ywg.ca) answers plain requests with a Cloudflare security page, so it was not read. The reach into north western Ontario and Nunavut is kept, carried by the airlines' own timetables.

claims.claim: numerous small remote communities across northern Manitoba on scheduled flights
claims.wasBefore: It also serves numerous small remote communities across northern Manitoba on scheduled flights.
claims.why: Merged into the Calm Air and Perimeter sentence, which the airlines' timetables carry. 'Numerous small remote' is Wikipedia's wording alone.

claims.claim: one of only nine Canadian airports with US preclearance
claims.wasBefore: Winnipeg is one of only nine Canadian airports with United States border pre-clearance
claims.why: The count no longer matches the authority: CBP (page modified 24 June 2026) lists ten preclearance locations in Canada, now including Billy Bishop Toronto, and gives Victoria's as a street address rather than an airport, so the number depends on what is counted. The preclearance itself is kept.

claims.claim: daily non-stop flights; seasonal services to Mexico
claims.wasBefore: Daily non-stop flights reach destinations across Canada and the United States, with seasonal services to Mexico and the Caribbean.
claims.why: 'Daily' and 'Mexico' have no current second source (see the softened claims); the rest of the sentence is kept.

claims.claim: hub for Calm Air, Perimeter and Cargojet
claims.wasBefore: It is a hub for Calm Air, Perimeter Airlines and the cargo carrier Cargojet
claims.why: Contradicted or unsupported by the airlines themselves: Cargojet's locations page labels Hamilton 'HUB OPERATIONS' and lists Winnipeg only as a station; Calm Air describes its hub-and-spoke network as run out of Rankin Inlet; Perimeter's pages do not use the word. Calm Air and Perimeter are still named, as airlines flying from here.

claims.claim: focus city for WestJet; base for Flair
claims.wasBefore: a focus city for WestJet and a base for Flair Airlines
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. flyflair.com answered with a Cloudflare security page (not retried in a browser); WestJet's own pages do not call Winnipeg a focus city. Softened to both airlines flying here.

claims.wasBefore: the Argentine architect Cesar Pelli with Stantec, drawing on Manitoba's prairie and sky
claims.why: Softened to 'Argentine-born' and to the prairie alone, which the architects' own page supports.

claims.claim: shares its 1,370 hectare site with CFB Winnipeg
claims.wasBefore: The airport shares its 1,370 hectare site with Canadian Forces Base Winnipeg.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. The RCAF's 17 Wing page describes CFB Winnipeg without mentioning the airport, OurAirports only lists 'CFB Winnipeg' as a search keyword, and the operator's site (the likely source for the 1,370 hectares) answers with a Cloudflare security page.

Held back: verified, but the old text had no passenger figure for it to replace. Total passengers (enplaned and deplaned) in 2025: the operator's preliminary quarterly statistics give 4,412,013; Statistics Canada's table gives 4,274,502 (about 3 per cent lower, as Statistics Canada counts only its surveyed air carrier traffic). Either supports 'more than 4.2 million passengers in 2025' if Andy wants it added. The operator's PDF was saved by grab.mjs directly (HTTP 200) before ywg.ca's HTML pages were found to be behind a Cloudflare security page.
